description: Small-displacement underbone motorcycle with a step-through frame, the most common vehicle on Thai roads.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small underbone step-through motorcycle, low central footboard, plastic leg shield and tank cover, single seat with a pillion grab rail, spoked wheels, upright handlebars with mirrors, chain guard and rear luggage rack Materials: Glossy plastic body panels with decal stripes, chrome exhaust and mirror stems, dusty spoked rims, worn black seat vinyl, chain grease at the sprocket.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Honda / Honda Motor. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 3,736/4,000 triangles, 3/8 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 3/8 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases at 0.7 MB, factory 85 ms. Twenty-two tube runs are built open, which is half the triangles of a capped one. Turntable: enclosed background is the step-through, the fork daylight and the gaps between the spokes, allowed on measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 0.712 x 1.258 x 1.891 m against a declared 0.71 x 1.25 x 1.92 -- within 1.6% on the longest axis and 0.6% on the other two. Stations off the proxy occupancy map: wheel centres at 0.15 L and 0.80 L (built z +0.64 and -0.58, a 1.22 m wheelbase), bars at 0.80 H = 1.00 m, mirror tips at 0.98 H = 1.258 m, seat top 0.60 H = 0.755 m, rack 0.545 H over 0.75-0.98 L, leg shield spanning 0.21-0.35 L.
featureReviews.notes: The first build read the same map at a wrong length and put the front axle 0.12 m back; the declared height of 1.07 was a list-time estimate to the bar tops and has been corrected to 1.25 with the proxy arithmetic in the registry notes.

featureReviews.evidence: Front end on 27 degrees of rake: chrome sliders THROUGH the front hub into navy shrouds, a triple clamp and lower yoke, a stem to the bar clamp, pulled-back bars with black grips, tall mirror stems to 0.124 m heads, a 0.146 m headlamp with a proud lens in the cowl between two amber pods, an instrument with a pale face, fender stays. Drivetrain: canted alloy barrel and finned head over a crankcase with two round covers, two chain runs to a rear sprocket under a navy chain guard, a dull #7a766f exhaust and silencer on the right, painted swingarm, shocks with chrome lowers, footpegs, kickstart and centre stand. Tail: a chrome rack of frame, rear rail, four struts and three slats, tail lamp on its bracket, two amber indicators on stalks, a black mudflap.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's forks missed the hub entirely and the exhaust was a bright chrome tube across the whole silhouette; the plate measures the silencer at #4d4137, so it is authored dull.

featureReviews.evidence: Two instanced OPEN wire wheels at one geometry: a closed tyre-ring lathe (16 segments), a rim ring, a 0.164 m drum hub with a chrome cap and eighteen three-sided prism spokes, with real daylight between them. Tread UVs are around-by-profile at 0.05 m per repeat (35 on a 0.556 m wheel); the rim, hub and spokes pin to the tile's white top 4% so their vertex colours render unmultiplied. Pivots wheel-front and wheel-rear on the axles.
featureReviews.notes: The first build used the CLOSED dished lathe, which is a solid disc that hides the spokes merged into it -- it scored 0.84 with two grey discs and a note claiming the spokes read as a lace.

featureReviews.evidence: Navy #343f58 as measured (plate #2b3551 lit, #1e2638 shaded), white pinstripes 4 mm proud on the covers and the rear fender edge, seat vinyl #4c4c4e, engine alloy #9b9c96 over a #63625e crankcase, chrome #b9bcbf, amber #b87a3a -- every tone off a plate crop. Two post-construction canvases: a dust multiplier on the paint and a tread on the rubber. The wrapped panels (shield, covers, seat, both fenders, cowl) are smooth-shaded below 34 degrees.
featureReviews.notes: Not lifted: the panels are thin and set against chrome and daylight. The tyre is authored 1.275x its measured tread against the tile's base of 200/255 and lifted to luma 105 for the back-lit frame.

notes: Budget class overridden from medium to large. At 1.92 m longest dimension the size rule says medium, which allows 2 draw calls and 2 materials -- not enough for a motorcycle, which needs the frame and wheels as bare metal separate from the painted plastic bodywork and the black seat and tyres. The bike is small but not simple, and the medium ceiling would force the wheels into the same material as the body. No destruction groups: it is a parking and traffic prop, not a breakable. Declared height corrected 1.07 -> 1.25 on 2026-08-28: the list-time 1.07 was to the bar tops, and the Meshy proxy (scratch/honda-wave/_ev, bbox 1.897 x 1.240 x 0.727) normalises to L:H:W 1 : 0.654 : 0.383, so at the declared 1.92 m length the mirror tips stand at 1.240/1.897 x 1.92 = 1.255 m and the width is 0.383 x 1.92 = 0.735. Built envelope 0.712 x 1.258 x 1.891.
